papers.summary: Argues that early resurrection belief is well supported but does not establish a literal, divinely caused resurrection unless the case compares the event with the complete weighted alternative space, states its prior assumptions, controls for dependent testimony, and supplies event-discriminating evidence.

papers.title: Scripture After the Fact - Context Swapping, Translation Drift, and the Manufacture of Messianic Fulfillment
papers.summary: Explains why context swapping, translation drift, poetic flattening, narrative control, selection, and shared literary causes can manufacture or inflate messianic fulfillment lists, and supplies a dependence-aware audit for distinguishing retrospective scriptural reuse from public predictive evidence.

papers.title: Sincere Seeking and Divine Hiddenness - 50
papers.summary: Argues that contradictory religious outcomes, cultural dependence, and apparently nonresistant nonbelief weaken a strong Christian sincere-seeking promise relative to ordinary human mediation without deductively disproving theism.

papers.title: Social Order Without a Moral Lawgiver - 43
papers.summary: Distinguishes moral seriousness, social order, moral objectivity, personal command, and public access, showing that each transition to a divine lawgiver requires independent evidence.

papers.title: Sufficient Reasons to Consider Leaving Christianity (version 1.3)
papers.summary: Fifty arguments that may give Christians good reason to reassess their beliefs.

papers.title: The Accommodation Burden - Divine Power, Human Understanding, and the Failure of Sacred Opacity
papers.summary: Argues that persistent public opacity is an evidential cost rather than a credential of transcendence under a Christian communicative model with complete audience knowledge, sufficient power, benevolent high-stakes concern, and an aim of finite uptake; without an independently supported offset, scalable intelligibility is more expected under that model while unstable uptake is more expected from finite human religious production.

papers.title: The Affective Core of Meaning - Against Normative Enrichment
papers.summary: Philosophical and theological traditions have consistently proposed normatively enriched conceptions of "meaningful" that add elements-virtue, rationality, purpose, divine alignment-beyond the affective state ordinary speakers report...

papers.title: The Alchemy of Ought - Tracing the Socio-Cognitive Reification of Human Rights
papers.summary: This paper challenges a strong metaphysical reading of human rights: the claim that rights are inherent, pre-political facts discoverable by reason and binding independent of human attitudes...

papers.title: The Alleged Resurrection and Bayesian Variables - Priors, Likelihoods, Dependence, and the Cost of a Specific Miracle Claim
papers.summary: Shows that public Bayesian arguments for Jesus' bodily resurrection cannot establish posterior superiority without independently constrained priors, joint likelihoods, source-dependence models, divine-intent assumptions, and a weighted alternative mixture.

papers.title: The Amalekite Infants - Divine Command, Collective Punishment, and the Collapse of Christian Moral Discernment
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Christian Ethics / Biblical Studies
papers.summary: Argues that a defense affirming divine authorization of intentional infant killing cannot retain the authorization, condemn equivalent rival commands, and use conduct as an independent test of divine goodness without a relevant portable difference.

papers.title: The Amoral Predicate Defense Non-Realist Evaluation, Pragmatic Language, and the Projection of Moral Weight
papers.category: Metaethics / Philosophy of Language / Philosophy of Religion
papers.summary: Argues explicitly from moral non-realism that sincere critical vocabulary does not require stance-independent moral facts: descriptive, end-relative, expressive, planning, and practice-internal readings can preserve genuine critical force, so separate semantic, metaethical, and theological bridges must be defended.

papers.title: The Architecture of Explanatory Satisfaction and the Affective Veto Against Stochastic Reality
papers.summary: The human intellect is driven by a voracious appetite for explanation, yet the criteria that generate "explanatory satisfaction" are frequently orthogonal to those required for epistemic accuracy...

papers.title: The Architecture of Explanatory Satisfaction and the Affective Veto Against Stochastic Reality - Why Satisfying Explanations Outrun Evidential Support
papers.category: Philosophy of Science / Psychology of Explanation

papers.title: The Asymptote of the Natural - Inductive Density and the A Posteriori Justification of Methodological Naturalism
papers.summary: The debate regarding Methodological Naturalism (MN) is stalled between "Essentialists" (who define science as naturalistic) and "Permissivists" (who view MN as bias)...

papers.title: The Attribute-Expectation Test Divine Love, Human Accessibility, and the Reasonableness of Demanding Public Clarity
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Divine Hiddenness / Religious Epistemology
papers.summary: Argues that maximal claims about divine love, knowledge, power, relationship, and communication generate defeasible public expectations; when the observed world repeatedly violates those expectations, flexible retrospective rescue weakens rather than protects the target God-concept.

papers.title: The Authority-Sampling Error - Quote Mining, Credibility Laundering, and the Stepping-Stone Fallacy in Theistic Argument
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Epistemology of Testimony
papers.summary: Argues that a critic’s authority supports only the proposition competently and contextually conveyed; further theistic or Christian conclusions require an independent bridge, especially when the source’s broader position resists the move.

papers.title: The Benevolent Monster - Age of Accountability, Infinite Utility, and the Soteriological Reductio of Infant Salvation
papers.summary: Develops a conditional reductio: under guaranteed pre-accountability salvation, adult irreversible-loss risk, and afterlife dominance, early death becomes soteriologically safer without licensing harm.

papers.title: The Bleeding Ideology - Interpretive Saturation, Doctrinal Priors, and the Capture of Evidential Space
papers.summary: Distinguishes unavoidable theory-ladenness from evidential capture. A public cumulative case does not confirm a Christian God-concept over a live rival when prayer, suffering, hiddenness, textual ambiguity, and disagreement receive their favorable direction only through flexible target-dependent interpretation and no independently constrained outcome or pattern bears a recognized anomaly cost. The conclusion is limited to that strategy, not Christianity or every form of religious warrant.

papers.title: The Borrowed Capital Fallacy - Presuppositionalism, Transcendental Overreach, and the Public Ownership of Rational Norms
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Christian Apologetics
papers.summary: Argues that a generic presuppositional borrowed-capital accusation used against a critic requires two independently defended bridges: Christianity's unique grounding of the exact rational norm and a critic-specific implication from norm-use plus actual commitments to Christianity. The slogan itself establishes neither bridge, so the accusation is not yet publicly justified, while local critiques and future transcendental arguments remain open.

papers.title: The Boundary-Retreat Device - No True Christian Reasoning, Identity Policing, and the Survival of Idealized Christendom
papers.summary: Argues that No True Christian reasoning becomes an evidential boundary retreat when current lives receive favorable credit but later countercases are erased; communities must accept either corrigible present classification or honest uncertainty under a lifelong-perseverance criterion.

papers.title: The Broken-World Lever - Discontent, Existential Friction, and the Apologetic Conversion of Unease into Doctrine
papers.summary: Critiques how Christian apologists manipulate human discontent to promote their theology

papers.title: The Buffer Zone Effect - Peripheral Controversy, Identity Maintenance, and the Avoidance of Core Theological Risk
papers.summary: Argues that victories in adjacent moral, scientific, and cultural controversies support Christianity’s distinctive claims only when an explicit bridge makes those victories more expected under Christianity than under live alternatives; explains how identity-protective reasoning can make weak transfer feel evidentially strong and provides a six-step audit for keeping conclusions proportional to evidence.

papers.title: The Calculus of Vice - A Fairness-Utility Model for Health Maintenance as a Civic Duty
papers.summary: As universal healthcare systems face increasing fiscal strain, the "asymmetric burden" of lifestyle-induced diseases has become a critical ethical flaw...

papers.title: The Cave-Design Error
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Natural Theology / Philosophy of Biology
papers.summary: Argues that complexity alone cannot identify agency because complex outcomes also arise under known non-agent mechanisms; replaces the shortcut with comparison of specified causal pathways, discriminating traces, and evidence capable of reversing the inference.

papers.title: The Certainty Dividend - Ambiguity Aversion, Identity Protection, and the Flight from Credence
papers.summary: Explains how certainty can deliver emotional and social returns that preserve confidence beyond the evidence, while distinguishing causal explanation from falsity and supplying symmetric calibration tests.

papers.title: The Circumvention Taxonomy - Infinite Worth, Divine Fiat, and the Failed Escape Routes of Penal Substitution
papers.summary: Tests the principal defenses of Penal Substitutionary Atonement against a two-part preservation requirement: each repair must independently justify both the transfer of culpability-grounded liability and completion of the stated penalty while retaining the doctrine's core claims.

papers.title: The Clarity Coercion Mistake - Divine Hiddenness, Doxastic Freedom, and the Difference between Evidence and Allegiance
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Divine Hiddenness
papers.summary: Argues that a generic free-will defense of divine hiddenness must show that every feasible non-dominating disclosure eliminates meaningful refusal. Clear evidence can constrain existence belief while leaving evaluation, allegiance, worship, obedience, protest, and resistance open; where punishment supplies the pressure, the threat rather than evidence does the coercive work. The conclusion is limited to this generic necessity inference.

papers.title: The Clarity Design Burden - Omniscience, Communicative Competence, and the Low Cost of Doctrinal Precision
papers.summary: Argues that generic human communication difficulty cannot excuse durable doctrinal ambiguity under an omniscient, competent, high-stakes clarity-aim authorship model because ordinary error controls were cheap and foreseeable; the resulting fragmentation consequently favors a human-historical literary model unless the target is revised or independently offset.

papers.title: The Competent Franchise: Liberal Epistemocracy and the Incentives of Civic Authority
papers.summary: Defends liberal epistemocracy through earned civic competence, competence-weighted political authority, citizens' chambers, leadership certification, and anti-capture constitutional safeguards.

papers.title: The Conditions of Moral Coherence - A Non-Realist Framework for Evaluating Moral Systems
The Dependency Inflation Problem - Formalizing Why Knowledge Does Not Presuppose God
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Epistemology
papers.summary: Argues that genuine epistemic dependence does not establish uniquely Christian metaphysical dependence, much less a knower's Christian belief or justification, without explicit relation, exclusivity, specificity, and attribution bridges.

papers.title: The Devil's in the Details-and So Is God - The Illogic of Dual-Agent Theism
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the explanatory structure of theistic ideologies that posit both a benevolent agent (God) and malevolent counterparts (demons and morally depraved humans) as exhaustive causes of worldly events...

papers.title: The Divine Judgment Evasion - Love, Judgment, and Semantic Collapse in Apologetic Defenses of Sacred Violence
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Christian Ethics / Problem of Evil
papers.summary: Argues that judgment, authority, mystery, and compensation do not publicly support perfect divine love unless they supply a victim-directed moral bridge and allow devastating treatment to bear some adverse evidential weight.

papers.title: The Documentary Delay - Papyri, Oral Memory, and the Evidential Cost of Late Gospel Composition
papers.summary: Distinguishes early resurrection belief from later event-level narrative detail and argues that material and oral explanations of documentary delay do not by themselves restore the comparative force that earlier independent controls would have supplied. The result is limited: it does not show the resurrection false or the Gospels worthless.

papers.title: The Documentation-Expectation Test Matthew's Earthquake, Raised Saints, and the Evidential Weight of Public Silence
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / New Testament Studies
papers.summary: Argues that Matthew 27:51–53's documentary isolation and scriptural-apocalyptic form favor a literary-apocalyptic reading over literal public reportage, while source loss prevents demonstrative disproof.

papers.title: The Eddy of Agency - Locating Subjective Will in an Objective Flow
keywords: Metaphysics of Free Will and Moral Responsibility
papers.summary: This paper proposes a naturalist reconciliation of objective determinism and subjective agency through the metaphor of the "Eddy." We argue that while human cognition is objectively determined, likened to a flow of material causation, it forms a recursive loop of processing that functions as a distinct subjective entity...

papers.title: The Elastic Hiddenness Defense - Ad Hoc Theodicy, Defense Mobility, and the Unfalsifiable Management of Divine Absence
papers.summary: This paper develops a methodological critique of hiddenness defenses. It is distinct from arguments that clearer evidence would not coerce free allegiance and from arguments that divine attributes generate expectations of accessibility.

papers.title: The Elastic Hiddenness Defense: Ad Hoc Theodicy, Defense Mobility, and the Unfalsifiable Management of Divine Absence
papers.summary: Distinguishes transparent revision from adequately supported revision through a five-step hypothetical exchange, a commitment ledger, constructive repair analogies, three separated probability questions, and a case-applied symbolic reconstruction. Clarifies the contested present-relationship premise and treats substantive philosophical alternatives fairly.

papers.title: The Evasion of Sacred Violence - 1 Samuel 15 - 3, Hyperbole, Deflection, and the Apologetic Relocation of Atrocity
papers.summary: Distinguishes incomplete replies, successful limited rebuttals, and evasive substitution in defenses of 1 Samuel 15. Paired examples and a sourced emergency-defense analysis preserve the force of cumulative evidence, warranted trust, and exhaustive alternatives.

papers.title: The Evidence-Mapping Illusion - Faith Rebranding, Social Calibration, and the Misdescription of Christian Belief Formation
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Social Epistemology
papers.summary: Argues that a common biblical pattern creates a faith gap whenever high Christian confidence exceeds the range warranted by total relevant evidence, while ordinary belief under uncertainty remains rational only when its degree changes with the evidence.

papers.title: The Evidential History of a Posterior - Update Trails, Path Integrity, and Doxastic Accountability
The Faith-Reversal Trap - Atheism-as-Faith Rhetoric, Burden Reversal, and the Self-Undermining Inflation of Faith
papers.summary: Argues that atheism-as-faith rhetoric is a semantic shell game: ordinary reliance is common but noncritical, evidential overbelief requires a symmetrical claim-level audit, and practical commitment governs action rather than belief.

papers.title: The Floating Fortress of Theology - Empirical Detachment, Hermeneutic Retreat, and the Public Failure of Christian Realism
papers.summary: Argues that a publicly realist theological claim earns warrant from a record only through a prospectively identifiable contrast with live alternatives, and that an unsupported revision which removes that contrast cannot inherit the stronger claim's evidential credit.

papers.title: The Generic Evidence Problem - Natural Theology, Rival Religious Uptake, and the Failure of Specific Confirmation
papers.summary: Argues that generic natural-theology data cannot specifically confirm Christianity without a demonstrated likelihood advantage over serious religious and nonreligious rivals, and supplies a disciplined evidence-routing test.

papers.title: The Gospel Payoff Fallacy Pragmatic Benefit, Epistemic Responsibility, and the Lowered Bar for Jesus
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Decision Theory
papers.summary: Argues that Craig's one-in-a-million stance is intrinsically irrational as a basis for belief: high stakes may rationalize action at low probability, but payoff cannot warrant belief, and strategic assent fails the Christian requirement of sincere inward belief.

papers.title: The Grammar of Credence - Evidential Alignment, Linguistic Modifiers, and the Gradient Hidden in Ordinary Belief
papers.category: Epistemology / Philosophy of Language / Philosophy of Religion
papers.summary: Argues that context-sensitive qualifiers publicly limit confidence and invited reliance: when a speaker crosses the evidential ceiling because certainty is important, comforting, or rewarded, the result is overstatement and, where that pressure causes the upgrade, epistemic laundering.

papers.title: The Gravity of Grammar - Binary Inertia and the Distortion of Epistemic Calibration
papers.summary: Language acts as a cognitive constraint, creating an inertia that pulls fallible, scalar thoughts toward binary assertions...

papers.title: The Hebrews 11 - 1 Puzzle - Interpretive Plurality, Faith-Function Drift, and the Failure of a Stable Epistemic Verse
papers.summary: This paper examines Hebrews 11:1 as a puzzle of interpretive plurality. It is distinct from earlier companion papers that analyzed semantic creep in the word faith and the illicit upgrade from assurance to public evidence.

papers.title: The Hebrews 11:1 Puzzle: Interpretive Plurality, Faith-Function Drift, and the Failure of a Stable Epistemic Verse
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Biblical Hermeneutics
papers.summary: Distinguishes legitimate interpretive plurality in Hebrews 11:1 from load-bearing movement among endurance, trust, confidence, evidence, substance, and practical commitment when no defensible bridge is stated or recoverable.

papers.title: The Historical Seed and the Mythic Husk - Minimal Jesus, Maximal Christology, and the Discipline of Not Overclaiming
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Historical Jesus / Christology
papers.summary: Argues that a minimally historical Jesus is more economical than total invention, while that modest conclusion supplies no automatic warrant for particular Gospel episodes, miracles, resurrection, or maximal Christology.

papers.title: The Honest Seeker's Duty - Critically Evaluating God-Concepts - 01
papers.summary: Argues that life-shaping religious allegiance carries a bounded duty of honest inquiry, separating evidence for a God-concept from warranted allegiance and reconstructing that duty in syllogistic and predicate--deontic form.

papers.title: The Hypostatic Union and the Law of Non-Contradiction - A Modal-Logical Audit
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophical Theology / Christology
papers.summary: A premise-sensitive modal-logical audit showing that Chalcedon alone does not entail contradiction, while specified unqualified extensions concerning omniscience, impeccability, human finitude, temptation, and modality are not jointly satisfiable.

papers.title: The Illusion of Divine Peace - Emotional Evidence and the Demand for Diagnosticity - 27
papers.summary: Argues that peace-like religious affect may be genuine and personally important yet lacks an independently validated feature that publicly identifies a specifically Christian source over serious religious and ordinary rivals.

papers.title: The Image of God Buffet - Semantic Overload, Hermeneutical Drift, and the Collapse of Imago Dei Clarity
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Theological Anthropology / Hermeneutics
papers.summary: Develops a three-link constraint test showing that an unspecified imago Dei premise cannot determine a public conclusion about dignity, rights, or policy until an interpretation and its descriptive and normative bridges are defended.

papers.title: The Immateriality Slide - Conscious Experience, Embodied Affect, and the Misclassification of the Spiritual
papers.category: Philosophy of Mind / Philosophy of Religion
papers.summary: Argues that the first-person depth, value, and explanatory irreducibility of love, reason, awe, and religious experience do not by themselves support an independent spiritual ontology; convergent intervention-sensitive dependence instead favors embodied accounts over that apologetic shortcut while leaving stronger dualist and religious proposals open to independent support.

papers.title: The Incentive Structure of Denial - Why Institutions Reward Non-Updating
The Incognito Failure Kierkegaard's King, Divine Hiddenness, and the Difference between Non-Coercion and Non-Recognition
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Divine Hiddenness
papers.summary: Argues that Kierkegaard's king-and-maiden parable supports non-coercive disclosure but cannot, by itself, justify recognition-blocking hiddenness; recognizable incognito does not explain nonbelief, while unrecognizable incognito prevents the conscious relationship it was meant to protect.

papers.title: The Incoherence of Eternal Damnation - Proportional Justice, Emotional Stability, and the Failure of Three Justifications - 32
papers.summary: Argues that final, punitive, irreversible grave postmortem harm fails the necessary aims of rehabilitation, proportionate retribution, and wrath-satisfaction unless the missing normative account is supplied or the model is changed.

papers.title: The Induction Ownership Fallacy - Hume, Theistic Appropriation, and the Illicit Conversion of a Shared Burden into an Apologetic Advantage
papers.category: Epistemology / Philosophy of Science / Philosophy of Religion
papers.summary: Argues that Hume's shared limit on deductive projection cannot be converted into an exclusive Christian warrant: a metaphysical explanation of order must still supply relevant stability, agent access, discriminating guidance, and a comparative case excluding rival routes.

papers.title: The Inductive Cherry Cosmic Origins, Selective Projection, and the Inductions Apologetics Leaves Behind
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophy of Science
papers.summary: Argues, through an eight-step house example and a wider evidential audit, that ordinary causal induction cannot by itself warrant a timeless, immaterial, personal creator when relevant patterns concerning minds, agency, time, and explanatory constraint are excluded without principled defeaters; strong domain transfer requires the full portfolio, while weak transfer removes the slogan's ordinary-evidence force.

papers.title: The Infinity Placeholder - Referents, Category Mistakes, and the Theological Misuse of Boundlessness
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophical Theology / Philosophy of Mathematics
papers.summary: Distinguishes seven structures concealed by theological infinity language and argues that a responsible claim must supply both a complete referent profile and a defensible bridge to its target conclusion, with focused applications to hiddenness, mystery, and endless punishment.

papers.title: The Inflation of Possibilities - Admissibility, Unknown Reserves, and the Discipline of Hypothesis Space
papers.category: Theology / Philosophy of Religion / Epistemology / Philosophy of Science
papers.summary: Argues that evidence may favor identified hypotheses without an exhaustive theory list, while absolute posteriors depend on a modeled partition and probability assigned to a residual category cannot be transferred to a favored member without an additional evidential bridge.

papers.title: The Intelligibility Gap - Modelability, Agency, and the Illicit Leap from Cosmic Order to God
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophy of Science / Natural Theology
papers.summary: Argues that cosmic modelability supports a specified agential origin only through entailment or a discriminating comparative expectation, and that modelability alone supplies neither route while leaving cumulative arguments open.

papers.title: The Managed Doubt Economy - Christian Doubt, Boundary Maintenance, and the Difference between Inquiry and Recommitment
papers.summary: Distinguishes open inquiry from doubt managed toward recommitment, separates credence from practical faith and belonging, illustrates five recurrent moves, and supplies symmetric standards for inquiry-honest Christian practice.

papers.title: The Manufacture of Genocide - Semantic Creep Institutional Legitimation and the Politics of the Ultimate Crime
papers.summary: Separates epistemic warrant, legal status, and social salience in genocide discourse; reconstructs how framing, conceptual compression, institutional relay, and procedural upgrading can manufacture apparent settlement; and defends proportionate prevention at serious risk without transferring preliminary claims into final judgments or collective guilt.

papers.title: The Mechanics of Non-Moral Civility - Evolutionary, Psychological, and Sociological Foundations of Social Order in the Absence of Moral Realism
papers.summary: A pervasive fear in both philosophical discourse and popular consciousness is that the rejection of moral realism, specifically the eliminativist stance that moral properties do not exist, must inevitably lead to societal collapse and individual debauchery...

papers.title: The Method-Selection Problem - Hermeneutical Buffets, Doctrinal Retrofitting, and the Search for a Stable Rule
papers.summary: Argues that when a preferred doctrine can select among accepted interpretive methods after the result is known, the resulting agreement is not independent scriptural warrant; proposes a six-part public ledger and cross-case test.

papers.title: The Millionth-Chance Standard - Pascalian Desperation, William Lane Craig, and the Collapse of Proportional Belief
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Decision Theory
papers.summary: Argues that Craig's one-in-a-million rule is intrinsically irrational as a basis for belief: high stakes may rationalize action at low probability, but payoff cannot warrant belief, and strategic assent fails the Christian requirement of sincere inward belief.

papers.title: The Miracle Audit - A Probabilistic Framework for Differentiating Anomalies from Supernatural Interventions
papers.summary: This paper proposes a rigorous epistemological framework for evaluating claims of supernatural intervention...

papers.title: The Missing Probability - Resurrection Apologetics, Unstated Priors, and the Failure of Comparative Explanation
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Resurrection / Bayesian Epistemology
papers.summary: Shows why explanatory fit is not posterior probability, distinguishes four commonly confused probability expressions, illustrates the issue with a familiar base-rate example and three hypothetical resurrection-sensitive cases, replaces one-at-a-time rival defeat with a complete non-resurrection comparator, and supplies a practical disclosure standard.

papers.title: The Modal Bridge Problem Conceivability, Greatness, and the Illicit Move from Concept to Instance
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Modal Logic / Metaphysics
papers.summary: Argues that a valid modal ontological derivation remains a conditional theorem rather than public evidence until its target-status, metaphysical-possibility, necessity, and discriminatory bridge premises receive independent and reciprocal warrant.

papers.title: The Moral Credentials of Divine Authority - 42
papers.summary: Argues that rational moral deference to a candidate divine authority requires a credentials case that is independent of the disputed claim, discriminates trustworthy from rival claimants, and remains correctable by adverse evidence.

papers.title: The Moral Grammar Exit - Eliminativist Moral Non-Realism, Pro-Social Evaluation, and the Replacement of Moralized Control
papers.summary: Compares realist, expressivist, fictionalist, and eliminativist policies for moralized public language and supplies an explicit translation protocol centered on harm, interests, consent, trust, power, evidence, and proposed action. The recommendation is conditional: prefer replacement only when useful functions survive and accountability improves.

papers.title: The Moral Realm Consolation - Emotional Unease, Normative Reification, and the Human Invention of Moral Furniture
papers.summary: Argues that the emotional and social usefulness of objective moral authority may explain robust realism's attraction but does not by itself warrant increased confidence in realism without comparative support or an independent truth-tracking bridge, while agents with specified aims can build practical protection under either ontology.

papers.title: The Moving Horizon - Artificial Intelligence and the Unbounded Expansion of Human Agency
papers.summary: Anxiety regarding artificial intelligence often stems from the assumption of a zero-sum tradeoff: as machines become more agentic, human agency and fulfillment must diminish...

papers.title: The Ontic Snap as a Cognitive Transition: Abductive Commitment and the Phase-Transition Hypothesis
papers.summary: Distinguishes a leading interpretation from its adoption as a working premise; relates abductive commitment to inductively learned expectations, separates findings from hypotheses, and specifies rival models and tests for a possible cognitive phase transition.

papers.title: The Ontological Slide - Value Hierarchies, Semantic Capture, and the Redefinition of God
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophy of Language
papers.summary: Argues that a highest practical value may organize a life and perform religion-like roles without thereby becoming a deity or establishing a specified form of theism; the functional reading is metaphysically thin, while the metaphysical reading lacks a defended bridge and discriminating evidence.

papers.title: The Outrage Trap - Justice, Moral Realism, and the Mistaking of Structural Failure for Ontological Fact
papers.summary: Argues that outrage at injustice can reveal harm and structural betrayal without by itself discriminating among metaethical theories or establishing a theistic ground.

papers.title: The Outsourced Rationality Argument - C. S. Lewis, Materialism, and the Apologetic Management of Ordinary Believers
papers.category: Philosophy of Mind / Epistemology / Philosophy of Religion
papers.summary: Argues that an argument from reason may pressure crude reductionism but cannot establish Christian theism, Christian ownership of rational norms, or a license to dismiss outsiders without additional defended premises.

papers.title: The Parsimonious World of the Moral Non-Realist - Illegitimate Questions, Surviving Values, and Life Without a Moral Realm
papers.summary: Develops a parsimonious, realm-denying moral non-realism in which moral-realm questions lose objective significance while subjective meaning, social density, law, coordination, vulnerability, and repair remain fully available as non-moral phenomena.

papers.title: The Pathologizing of Doubt: Evidence Poverty, Deconstruction, and Pastoral Diagnosis in Frank Turek's Apologetics Podcast Corpus
papers.summary: Distinguishes explanations of religious doubt from supported, relevant, and proportionate assessments of its reasons, using eight contextual podcast cases, worked examples, and an annotated formal reconstruction.

papers.title: The Phenomenology of Certainty - Why Felt Sureness Is Not Evidence
The Pistis Proof Burden - Hebrews 11 - 1, Greek Semantic Range, and the Illicit Upgrade from Assurance to Evidence
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Biblical Critique
papers.summary: Argues that even an assurance-, proof-, or evidence-like reading of Hebrews 11:1 does not itself establish faith's unseen object: assurance must travel through a reliable, claim-specific, rival-discriminating, and defeater-sensitive bridge, with a further transmission step for public warrant.

papers.title: The Predictive Power of Religions' Popularity - 14
papers.summary: Argues that testimony can transmit warrant while correlated religious headcount adds no independent public confirmation beyond its sources, because incompatible convictions, cultural inheritance, persistent nonconvergence, cross-tradition cohesion, and a thin calibrating track record fit ordinary-transmission sufficiency better than a single publicly clarity-seeking Christian revelation.

papers.title: The Proper Basicality Load - Plantinga, Basic Belief, and the Categorical Burden of Doctrinally Thick Theism
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Epistemology
papers.summary: Argues that proper basicality for thin theism does not automatically transmit warrant to a doctrinally thick Christian package: every indispensable component needs either a truth-aimed noninferential source or a warranted inferential or testimonial bridge.

papers.title: The Prophecy Marker Problem - 2 Timothy 3, Vague Traits, and the Failure of Apocalyptic Measurement
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Biblical Hermeneutics / Eschatology
papers.summary: Argues that the vice list in 2 Timothy 3 can function as moral exhortation but not as a clock: its traits lack definitions, baselines, demonstrated change, and temporal discrimination, while the passage itself applies the pattern to contemporaries.

papers.title: The Providence Deferral - God Has a Plan, Non-Testable Consolation, and the Ethics of Unverifiable Meaning
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Problem of Evil
papers.summary: Argues that an unconstrained hidden-plan appeal cannot gain public explanatory or confirmatory force from events it does not prospectively rank; mystery must suspend matched positive and negative evidential inferences, while personal hope and invited consolation remain distinct speech acts.

papers.title: The Puppeteer Mind - Dualism, Neural Dependence, and the Explanatory Redundancy of Immaterial Control
papers.category: Philosophy of Mind / Metaphysics / Mental Causation
papers.summary: Argues that neural dependence establishes the brain's causal relevance but does not discriminate an instrument-mediated controller from a no-controller account; the added controller gains incremental public causal-explanatory support only through a distinctive difference or independent evidence.

papers.title: The Purpose-Package Trap - Youth, Existential Vulnerability, and the Capture of Meaning-Making
papers.summary: Argues that purpose guidance becomes exploitative when a duty-bearing authority uses a young person's developmental or relational dependence to obstruct inquiry, comparison and delay, revision, or safe exit.

papers.title: The Reliability Relay - C. S. Lewis, Cognitive Trust, and the Christian Retreat to Empirical Testing
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Cognitive Reliability
papers.summary: Distinguishes metaphysical enabling, global warrant, and local calibration, then documents how Christians use developmental, clinical, safeguarding, financial, textual, and argumentative tests to decide which cognitive performances to trust. Because confidence changes with those tests while the Christian-origin premise remains fixed, the tests supply the local discrimination unless theology predicts an independently supported difference.

papers.title: The Romans 1 - 20 Testimony Gap - General Revelation, Cross-Cultural Evidence, and the Missing Archive of Clear Perception
papers.summary: Romans 1:20 is often read as a sweeping epistemic claim: God's invisible qualities, eternal power, and divine nature are clearly perceived from creation, leaving human beings without excuse. This paper asks what public evidence should exist if that claim is true in the robust apologetic sense.

papers.title: The Romans 1:20 Testimony Gap: General Revelation, Cross-Cultural Evidence, and the Missing Archive of Clear Perception
papers.summary: Generic religious reports and disagreement, even considered together, do not adequately justify a universal accusation of suppressed creator-knowledge and guilt. The paper distinguishes belief, knowledge, access and responsibility, with concrete examples and qualified absence-of-evidence calculations.

papers.title: The Semantic Creep of Faith - Hebrews 11 - 1, Translation Drift, and the Rebranding of Belief
papers.summary: Argues that Hebrews 11:1 cannot, by translation alone, convert trust, assurance, conviction, or evidence-like language into public warrant; an explicit semantic and evidential bridge is required.

papers.title: The Silence of Heaven - Assessing Answers to Prayer - 10
papers.summary: Argues that controlled distant-intercession evidence weighs against recurring public-effect models of petitionary prayer and proposes a preregistered multisite equivalence-and-Bayesian test capable of yielding a decisive bounded null.

papers.title: The Sophistical Question - Loaded Theistic Questions, Burden Shifts, and the Rhetorical Defense of Faith
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Informal Logic / Argumentation Theory
papers.summary: Argues that a loaded theistic question supplies no independent religious evidence until its hidden premises, narrowed options, unstable terms, misplaced categories, or unequal burdens are repaired and its favored answer is comparatively defended.

papers.title: The Spirit in the Closed Circuit - Why Catholic Authority Does Not Solve the Problem of Discernment
papers.summary: Argues that Lundahl's Catholic discernment criteria can regulate belief but cannot identify the Holy Spirit, and specifies the public loss conditions and comparative tests required to establish his authority, miracle, Pentecost, and fruits claims.

papers.title: The Status of Methodological Naturalism as Justified by Precedent
papers.summary: 方法論的自然主義は、科学的方法論における不可欠なヒューリスティクス(発見的方法)とし て、その重要性をますます高めている。同理論を採用した科学の成功例、及び同理論のもたら す制約の効率性を鑑みるに、方法論的自然主義の活用は今後も必要不可欠と考えられる。本稿 においては、方法論的自然主義の出現の歴史、現在の状況と、常に難解かつ反直観的である科 学研究の分野での利用に関する将来的展望について検討する。 Methodological naturalism has increasingly proven its worth as an essential heuristic in scientific methodology...

papers.title: The Substitution Problem - Formal Equivalence, Punishment Transfer, and the Collapse of Atonement Proportionality
papers.summary: This paper argues that penal substitution requires two distinct bridge principles: a transfer rule explaining why treatment of an innocent substitute can discharge liability grounded in an offender's culpable act, and a sanction-fit rule explaining why Christ's finite, voluntary, and victorious passion relevantly matches the punishment assigned to sinners. Legal imputation, voluntariness, corporate participation, infinite worth, and governmental equivalence each clarify part of the model, but standard Penal Substitutionary Atonement has not yet jointly justified both bridges. The conclusion is conditional rather than a disproof of every future version or of non-penal atonement models.

papers.title: The Suspended Web of Induction - How the Brain's Attention to Regularities Matures into Reliable Knowledge
papers.summary: Argues that the brain's sensitivity to regularities develops into a revisable inductive web that governs personal judgment and scientific inquiry by rewarding predictive success without demanding certainty or final ontology.

papers.title: The Therapeutic Contradiction - Suffering, Medicine, Providence, and the Practical Rejection of Redemptive Pain
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophy of Medicine / Medical Ethics
papers.summary: Argues that Christian medical relief supplies practical moral evidence against necessity-based theodicies when the same preventable suffering is justified by goods said to require it and no principled difference between divine and human duties is supplied.

papers.title: The Threshold of the Real - Inductive Density and the Emergence of the Human Ontic
papers.summary: Traditional realism posits that objects exist independently of observers, while anti-realism argues they are constructed...

papers.title: The Trajectory of Christianity's Track Record for Claims About the Natural World - 15
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / History of Science
papers.summary: Argues that Christianity's selected natural-world record across astronomy, creationism, intercessory prayer, and possession-related care fits ordinary cultural development better than a model predicting specially reliable revelation, while limiting the conclusion to that evidential use.

papers.title: The Two-Gap Theory of Irrationality - Evidence Perception, Belief Integrity, and Diagnostic Repair
The Unavoidability Maneuver Faith Inflation, Evidential Proportionality, and the Choice to Outrun Evidence
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Religious Epistemology / Epistemology
papers.summary: Argues that the claim that faith is unavoidable succeeds only by shifting between ordinary fallible reliance, evidentially excessive confidence, and practical commitment; uncertainty can require action without licensing belief beyond the evidence.

papers.title: The Unknowns Reserve as Epistemic Norm - Bayesian Humility in Historical Miracle Claims
papers.summary: Bayesian reasoning provides a rigorous framework for evaluating extraordinary claims, yet it is only as sound as the assumptions encoded in priors, likelihoods, and model structure...

papers.title: The Valuation Problem in Justice Theory - Incommensurability and the Categorical Failure of PSA - 35
papers.summary: Argues that a finite passion does not establish completion of an essentially durational penalty through infinite worth alone unless the account supplies an equivalence rule or revises its completion conditions.

papers.title: The Virtue of 'I Don't Know' - Uncertainty as a Rational Alternative to Faith - 25
papers.summary: Argues that existential uncertainty supplies no truth-directed bridge to categorical faith in a specific God-concept, so calibrated credence or suspended judgment better preserves symmetry and inquiry absent discriminating evidence or independent warrant.

papers.title: The Weaponization of Nothing - Cosmological Equivocation, Absolute Absence, and the Apologetic Misuse of Scientific Terms
papers.category: Philosophy of Religion / Philosophy of Cosmology / Scientific Language
papers.summary: Shows that identifying a scientific use of ‘nothing’ as physically structured can correct misleading language but cannot, without independent causal, modal, agency, and comparative premises, refute the model or favor a theistic explanation.

papers.title: The Widening Gap - Employment Opportunities for Workers with and without AI Skills in the Next 5 and 20 Years
papers.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping the global labor market, creating measurable disparities in employment opportunities between workers equipped with AI skills and those without...

papers.title: The Wormwood of Penal Substitution and the Miscarriage of Justice - 34
papers.summary: Argues that literal retributive penal substitution requires a responsibility-making bridge that gives an innocent Christ genuine penal desert; consent and civil substitution do not supply it, while accounts that revise punishment into sacrifice, satisfaction, solidarity, repair, or consequence become nonretributive.

papers.title: Theological Preclearance: Source-Indexed Moral Judgment, Retrofitting, and the Logic of Protected Divine Goodness
papers.summary: Shows why a protected moral-test outcome supplies no fresh confirmation of a favored revelation, while distinguishing relevant evidence, unresolved answers and justified revision through worked comparisons and probability examples.

papers.title: Unknowns Without Supernatural Default - 46
papers.summary: Defends the no-transfer principle: defeat of current natural models is not a donation of support to a supernatural rival; positive support requires evidence that comparatively favors the specified target over error, misdescription, unknown mechanisms, and other live alternatives.

papers.title: Useful Fictions Common in Philosophical Pedagogy
papers.summary: Philosophical education relies on a gradient of "lies to children"-simplified heuristics that facilitate initial understanding but ultimately fail under rigorous scrutiny...

papers.title: Villain-Driven Irrationality: How Hating a Target Weakens Evidence, Justice, and Dissent
papers.summary: Defines a target-conditioned villain exception, distinguishes it from legitimate priors and precaution, and shows how double counting, social amplification, and vice transfer can weaken evidence, justice, and dissent.

papers.title: Warranted Uncertainty - The Discipline of Not Knowing in a Credence-First Epistemology
When Ask and You Shall Receive Fails
papers.summary: Argues that an unrestricted every-outcome interpretation supplies no public confirmation of dependable petitionary intervention, while the reviewed clinical evidence and flexibly attributed ordinary cases provide no robust independent advantage; occasional opaque answers and prayer's relational or coping value remain open.

papers.title: When Every Outcome Is an Answer - Answer-Inflation, Diagnostic Content, and the Semantics of Petitionary Prayer
papers.summary: Argues that a retrospective rule capable of calling every possible prayer outcome an answer cannot by itself make an observed result public evidence for one token answered-prayer claim; content-linkage, contrastive difference, and prospective identifiability are required, while prayer's relational value and independently supported theology remain open.

papers.title: When Inerrancy Becomes Moot - Coherence, Conceptual Contradiction, and the Limits of Textual Perfection
papers.summary: Argues conditionally that scriptural inerrancy cannot by itself warrant a disputed doctrine unless a justified interpretation identifies determinate affirmed content and that content is jointly satisfiable under the logic being used.

papers.title: When Love Loses Meaning - Semantic Inversion and Divine Claims - 05
papers.summary: Develops a conditional semantic trilemma for a specified Christian God-concept: revise a harmful divine attribution, supply a constrained love-compatible justification, or acknowledge weaker continuity with ordinary personal love.

papers.title: Where Is the Conscious Subject - A Dynamical Criterion for System Boundaries
papers.summary: Develops a non-circular, boundary-first criterion for consciousness research that identifies inclusion-minimal, dynamically autonomous systems before theory-specific measurement, with explicit tests for role completeness, separability, constitutive components, and cross-specification stability.

papers.title: Would a God of Clarity Have Written the Bible - 03
papers.summary: Argues in an accessible cumulative case that structured Christian disagreement is more expected under ordinary historical transmission than under a strong Bible-centered divine clarity claim.

papers.title: Would a Holy Book Omit Essential Elements of Rational Thought and Belief - 07
papers.summary: Argues that the Bible's mixture of valuable local checks and no integrated, symmetric, self-applying calibration method provides moderate comparative support for historical-human development over a strong divine-pedagogy model.

papers.title: Would a Rational God Endorse Faith Beyond Evidence - 22
papers.summary: Distinguishes trust, hope, commitment, and noninferential warrant from overbelief, arguing that a rational, truth-committed deity would not endorse confidence exceeding total truth-directed warrant as rational belief.
